youtube.title: The Titanic Was Warned 6 Times. Here's What Happened to Every Warning
youtube.description:
On 14 April 1912, the Titanic received at least six ice warnings. One sat in the White Star chairman's pocket. Two never reached the bridge. The last was cut off with the words "shut up." This is the story of every warning, the ship that watched the rockets, and the rules the disaster left behind.

0:00 Shut up
0:55 Unsinkable
2:07 Six warnings
3:20 Iceberg, right ahead
4:29 The ship that watched
5:44 What the file tells us

Sources:
British Wreck Commissioner's Inquiry report, Messages section: https://www.titanicinquiry.org/BOTInq/BOTReport/botRepMessages.php
US Senate Inquiry testimony (Rostron): https://www.titanicinquiry.org/USInq/AmInq01Rostron01.php
Britannica, Titanic: Aftermath and investigation: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Titanic/Aftermath-and-investigation
MAIB reappraisal of the SS Californian evidence (1992).

Images: Wikimedia Commons, public domain (1912 photographs; New York Times front page; US Coast Guard).
Narration voice: AI.

📂 The 60-second version: Case File #036.
